detail:
StatPearls describes vasovagal syncope as typically treated conservatively. When triggers are known and avoidable, patients are instructed to avoid them; they are also instructed to drink more fluids to improve volume status and to change positions slowly. Learning the prodrome, the warning symptoms that precede an episode, matters because sitting or lying down early can prevent a full faint and the injuries that come with falling.

The 2017 ACC/AHA/HRS syncope guideline adds physical counterpressure maneuvers, tensing the legs, arms, or abdomen during the warning phase, as a useful option for people with a long enough prodrome, and describes medicines such as midodrine for selected recurrent cases. Frequent, injurious, or warning-free faints need specialist evaluation rather than self-management.

Talk to your doctor before starting or changing any medication.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material.
summary: StatPearls describes conservative management first: avoiding known triggers, drinking more fluids to support blood volume, and changing positions slowly, with medicines reserved for selected people with frequent episodes.
takeaways: most episodes are managed conservatively, without daily medicine
extra fluids support blood volume; ask your doctor about amounts
lying down at the first warning signs can prevent a full faint
frequent faints need a doctor's review, not self-treatment
title: Managing vasovagal episodes
